executiveSummary: GM0569's official 2025 identity, contained centre, 29,521 residents, 37 neighbourhoods, seven BAG places, seventeen settlement labels and four numbered-road links are coherent; neighbourhood population differs by only nine residents (+0.03%) and is reconciled without rewriting source observations. The deterministic ten-preset, six-checkpoint, eight-service contract passes. Release is nevertheless correction-required. Nieuwkoop is a low peat-polder and lake municipality whose flood pathways depend on regional defences, Rijnland's boezem, the Ringsloot, daily pumping, many public/private underdrainage systems and cross-water-board boundaries. The simulator instead produces exact 1.242420 coastal and 0.605144 river inundation stress, affected populations and service curves without selecting a defence failure, hydraulic connectivity, arrival, pumping or dewatering case. River, coastal, pluvial, heat and wildfire maps reuse the exact same leading neighbourhood order; a controlled fire at the CBS Nieuwkoopse Plassen neighbourhood centre ranks that source only 26th of 37. The four-edge road graph omits the N multiline/local access, bridge and village network that links dispersed settlements and external acute care, while the current municipal page reports a valid-time Zevenhovenseweg closure but the deployed NDW municipality assignment contains no situation. Public registers expose 332 partial water-control/wastewater points, 38 antenna installations, twelve education records and one Liander planning sample, but none proves live topology, backup, outage, capacity or restoration. No acute-care department and no RWS Waterinfo observation/forecast are assigned inside GM0569. Every absence/null remains Unknown or NoData, never zero, safe, open, available or restored.

evidenceSources.publisher: Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek / PDOK / Kadaster
evidenceSources.title: E01 — GM0569 official 2025 municipality, neighbourhood, place and settlement geography and statistics
evidenceSources.edition: CBS Wijken en buurten 2025; BAG/PDOK/BRT snapshots retrieved 31 August 2026
supports: Annual CC BY 4.0 CBS/PDOK input identifies GM0569 as Nieuwkoop in Zuid-Holland and reports 29,521 residents, density 376/km2, 23.1% aged 65 or older and 3,602 one-person households. The generated centre [4.7865791755881215, 52.17353471893337] lies inside the 2025 generalized boundary.

Thirty-seven neighbourhood rows in thirteen districts sum to 29,530 residents, nine above the municipality total (+0.03%); households sum to 12,315 and independently rounded age-65-plus rows to 6,810. Deterministic allocation reconciles exactly to 29,521 without altering source observations.

BAG supplies seven current woonplaatsen and all reference points are contained: Nieuwkoop, Nieuwveen, Noorden, Ter Aar, Vrouwenakker, Woerdense Verlaat and Zevenhoven. BRT supplies seventeen settlement labels: twelve woonkernen, three buurtschappen and two deelkernen.

All 37 rows have age, population, household, land and water fields, but average home value/tenure covers 26/37, cars per household 23/37, benefit fields 28/37, GP/supermarket distance 35/37 and district heating/public charging 0/37. Null, suppression, not-applicable and published zero remain distinct.

evidenceSources.title: E02 — Municipal sewer/climate programme and documented extreme-rain experience
evidenceSources.edition: Beleids- en beheerplan waterpartijen 2025–2029; GRP 2021–2025 and 2019–2020 stress-test evidence retained as dated inputs
supports: The current water-body plan links municipal water management to the earlier sewer programme and climate change. The municipality's commissioned stress tests map heat, drought and water-nuisance bottlenecks; the machine-readable cells, exact scenarios and licence are not present in the deployed model.

The official GRP records approximately 60 mm in one hour at Ter Aar in May 2018 and 130 mm over several hours in September 2018, when the overall water system was full and complaints occurred in Nieuwkoop, Ter Aar and Nieuwveen. Historic events establish mechanisms and validation cases, not current rainfall or present damage.

The GRP identifies investigations at Sportvelden/Roerdomplaan/Het Brak-Joris Zudde in Nieuwkoop, Oostkanaalweg in Ter Aar and Korte Meentweg in Woerdense Verlaat, and notes that pressure/vacuum sewers in the outside area are not designed for stormwater. Plans and investigations do not prove completed works, capacity or event-time drainage state.

No blanket machine-layer reuse licence or update cadence was identified for the reviewed stress-test material; source edition, scenario, CRS/resolution, coverage and NoData must therefore remain explicit.

evidenceSources.title: E03 — Gemaal Nieuwkoop and the Nieuwkoop–Zevenhoven polder/boezem mechanism
evidenceSources.edition: Current public authority page inspected 3 September 2026; operational state remains unobserved
supports: Rijnland describes the low Nieuwkoopse en Zevenhovense Polder at a managed water level of NAP -5.90 m with substantial seepage and required daily pumping. This is static system evidence, not a measured municipality elevation or current level.

About 60% of the polder uses underdrainage; private installations discharge into the polder boezem/Ringsloot and the main Nieuwkoop pumping station discharges into Rijnland's boezem, which in turn drains toward sea through boezem pumping stations.

Rijnland explicitly calls the many underdrainage installations vulnerable during extreme precipitation and dependent on communication and cooperation among many private parties. One municipality flood scalar cannot represent this control chain.

The page reports a 2,773 ha service area and a rebuilt electric pumping station, but does not establish present settings, power/backup, reserve, connected cell, obstruction, operator action or T+72 recovery.

evidenceSources.title: E04 — Regional Risk Profile and municipality risk context for Nieuwkoop
evidenceSources.edition: Current online municipality profile and public regional risk-profile PDF inspected 3 September 2026
supports: VRHM identifies Nieuwkoop as a rural Groene Hart municipality with thirteen residential cores, extensive lake/Natura 2000, agricultural and recreation areas, and boundaries with Veiligheidsregio Utrecht and Amsterdam-Amstelland. Cross-region assistance and information are material first-72-hour dependencies.

The regional profile distinguishes primary-defence failure from regional-defence failure. It says regional defences can fail through high boezem levels or instability and can seriously damage buildings and infrastructure; it does not select a GM0569 breach or depth.

VRHM lists extreme cold/snow/ice, heat/smog, drought, wind/storm and extreme rain, with impact varying strongly locally. It separately lists forest, dune, heath, reed and peat fires and notes reed fires among the region's more frequent nature fires.

The risk inventory is strategic planning evidence. It does not establish a current warning, incident, affected footprint, route, vehicle, responder, shelter, hospital acceptance, pump action or restoration. No blanket machine reuse licence was identified.

evidenceSources.title: E05 — Nieuwkoop peat/lake landscape, Natura 2000 management and subsidence
evidenceSources.edition: Current provincial area page and Natura 2000 management plan 2025–2031 inspected 3 September 2026
supports: The province identifies Nieuwkoopse Plassen & De Haeck as Natura 2000 and lists water quality, habitat, nitrogen and limiting peat subsidence as linked area tasks; water-infiltration systems are being installed around the lakes.

The 2025–2031 plan describes an inversion landscape: remaining lake peat generally at NAP -1 to -1.5 m, surrounding peat meadows roughly NAP -1.5 to -2.5 m and Polder Nieuwkoop locally near NAP -5.5 m. These are plan-scale ranges, not a substitute for AHN terrain or incident water levels.

The plan says warmer, drier summers increase water-inlet need and accelerate peat oxidation/subsidence, particularly in Meijeraslanden and Polder Westveen. This supports distinct drought/subsidence/water-quality cases rather than a generic heat percentage.

Combining the local peat/reed landscape with VRHM's fire classes supports a plausible local peat/reed-fire pathway as an inference; it does not prove ignition, fuel moisture, perimeter, smoke, visitor presence, firewater or suppression.

evidenceSources.publisher: Rijkswaterstaat / ProRail / OVapi / RIVM / Provincie Zuid-Holland / Gemeente Nieuwkoop
evidenceSources.title: E06 — Road, transit, bridge, current restriction and external acute-care dependencies
evidenceSources.edition: NWB-Light 1 August 2026; ProRail/GTFS snapshots 31 August 2026; RIVM questionnaire v1.1 published 3 July 2026; current municipal works page inspected 3 September 2026
supports: The monthly CC0 NWB logical graph gives four cross-boundary links: two non-additive N231 sections toward Alphen aan den Rijn/Uithoorn, N446 toward Kaag en Braassem and N460 toward Alphen. It omits local streets, N463/other cross-region access, bridges, water crossings and internal village routes and uses generalized scenario-unit capacity 150.

Nieuwkoop's transport plan describes traffic using N231/N207/N446 and Ringdijk-Hertog van Beijerenstraat, including the Noorden/Woerdense Verlaat relationship with N463. Provincial evidence calls N231 an important route for Aalsmeer/Schiphol and agricultural traffic. Identity is supported; incident capacity/passability is not.

The municipality currently reports Zevenhovenseweg in Ter Aar closed to motor vehicles from 17 August through 18 September 2026. The deployed NDW snapshot assigns no current situation to GM0569; absence from that bounded feed is not an open road and the municipal notice requires segment/time matching before simulation effect.

No ProRail passenger station and no RIVM acute-care department lies inside GM0569; GTFS has 72 stop areas. Nearest straight-line reference records are Ziekenhuis Amstelland 14.588 km (limited hours), Alrijne Leiderdorp 16.850 km, AMC 17.847 km, Groene Hart Gouda 17.857 km and Spaarne Hoofddorp 19.084 km; all but Amstelland report 24/7 emergency care. Distances are not travel times, route availability or acceptance.

evidenceSources.publisher: Het Waterschapshuis / Netbeheer Nederland / RDI / DUO
evidenceSources.title: E07 — Partial water assets, grid planning, communications and education context
supports: The partial CC BY-SA 4.0 HWH aggregation contains 332 GM0569 points: 149 surface-water pumps, 157 weirs, nineteen sluices, six sewer pumps and AWZI Nieuwveen. Capacity is present for 62 surface pumps and all six sewer pumps, absent for 87 surface pumps, all weirs/sluices and the treatment point; manager records span Rijnland, De Stichtse Rijnlanden and Amstel, Gooi en Vecht.

Point containment can legitimately include objects belonging to three water managers near jurisdictional boundaries. It does not prove network ownership at every cell, connected catchment, compatible capacity unit, flow direction, settings, operation, backup or restoration.

One postcode sample maps to Liander service area OS NIEUWKOOP 10-1i and reports planning/load/queue fields and projects from 2026. Its own metadata says this is a large-user planning sample, not municipality coverage, a substation location, live load, outage, switching, reserve or restoration.

RDI contains 38 antenna installations and DUO twelve education records. Registered location/application does not establish radio coverage/backhaul/power, shelter status, occupants, accessibility, supplies, generator endurance or live operation. RDI's WFS states no reuse licence/cadence; DUO is daily under CC Attribution, version unspecified.

evidenceSources.publisher: Rijkswaterstaat Waterinfo / KNMI / Nationaal Dataportaal Wegverkeer
evidenceSources.title: E08 — Timestamped observation/forecast coverage and explicit NoData
evidenceSources.edition: Waterinfo observations retrieved 2 September 2026 18:03Z and forecasts 3 September 2026 04:29Z; KNMI/NDW snapshots retrieved 2–3 September 2026
supports: No Waterinfo observation or forecast point is assigned inside GM0569. Waterinfo is generally ten-minute public context, CC0 unless otherwise stated, with declining forecast coverage and no national T+72 return; no assigned point is NoData, never zero level/discharge or safety.

One KNMI station named Nieuwkoop is assigned at reported station height -5.77 m. At 2 September 23:30Z it reports wind 4.43 m/s and gust 7.44 m/s, while temperature, humidity and rainfall are null. A sparse station point is not a municipal field or T+72 forecast; null rain is NoData, not zero rain.

No NDW current situation is assigned to GM0569 in the inspected snapshot despite the separate current municipal road-closure notice. DATEX coverage/geometry and authority notices need explicit reconciliation; neither source alone establishes every road open or closed.

Waterinfo/NDW are CC0 unless component exceptions apply and KNMI observations are CC BY 4.0. Every item must retain observation/publication/issue/valid/retrieval time, spatial support, coverage, affectsSimulation=false and NoData until a governed scenario adapter binds it.

The municipality centre and all seven BAG reference points lie inside the generalized boundary.

Every map needs publisher, version, CRS/resolution, scenario/valid time, coverage, uncertainty, licence and NoData; uncovered cells are not zero.

Neighbourhood population is 29,530 (+9, +0.03%); households total 12,315 and rounded age-65-plus rows 6,810. Source observations remain unchanged.

settlements.summary: Seven BAG places and seventeen BRT settlement labels are contained and retained with independent source roles.

The VRHM narrative uses thirteen residential cores, a planning concept that does not need to numerically equal BAG woonplaats or BRT settlement counts.

transport.summary: Four numbered-road proxies cannot represent dispersed-village, bridge, cross-region, closure, transit and external-care access.

There is no local passenger station; 72 GTFS stop areas establish scheduled identity only. Static stops do not prove vehicle operation, capacity, accessibility, passengers or restoration.
The valid-time Zevenhovenseweg closure is absent from the assigned NDW snapshot. Route state must reconcile authoritative notices by segment/time; missing NDW is not open road.
External acute-care choices require different corridor/cross-region paths, current acceptance and diversion; straight-line distance is not ambulance time.

emergencyContext.summary: Strong public risk and asset context exists, but incident-time water, route, care, utility and resource state remains unknown.

HWH, RDI, DUO, RIVM, NBNL, KNMI, Waterinfo and NDW are explicitly context and affectsSimulation=false. Register/plan presence is not operational availability.
No public source reviewed provides complete privacy-safe first-72-hour staffing, pumps/backup, shelters, buses/boats, care acceptance, fuel, food/medicine stock, utility switching or repair progress.

scenarioMatrix.summary: All ten canonical presets ran deterministically at T+0/6/12/24/48/72 across all eight services.
notes: Focused MUNICIPALITY_AUDIT_CODE=GM0569 coverage passes both tests.
Every snapshot contains finite bounded hazard/service values and the app scenario factory matches the canonical presets.
Numerical contract success is not validation of local physical calibration or operational truth.

numericalInvariants.summary: Population, demand, delivery, route invariance, cumulative deprivation, causal and deterministic invariants pass.

spatialPlausibility.summary: Generic municipal forcing and a shared neighbourhood seed contradict Nieuwkoop's mechanism-specific geography.
notes: At T+24 river, coastal, pluvial, heat and wildfire all rank Langeraar, Schoterhoek, Schoterveld, Nieuwveen Buitengebied Oost, Nieuwkoop Buitengebied West and Zevenhoven Buitengebied Oost first through sixth in exactly the same order.

A controlled wildfire source at the official CBS centre of Nieuwkoop Nieuwkoopse Plassen ranks that source cell 26th of 37, behind the same generic leaders, despite nonzero direct municipal flame/smoke.
The maps do not encode Rijnland boezem/defences, low polders and higher lake peat, historical rain bottlenecks, built-form heat, peat/reed fuel, wind or named cyber targets.

serviceDependencies.summary: Exact service percentages are unsupported by physical water, utility, access, care and supply topology.
notes: River T+24 emits exact availability from Drainage 0.638092 to Mobility 0.914575; coastal T+24 ranges from Drainage 0.382636 to Supply 0.866513 without asset intersection or operator state.
The documented underdrainage–Ringsloot–main pump–boezem chain, sewer/wastewater separation, cross-manager objects and power dependence are not causally represented.
One Liander planning sample, 38 antenna sites, twelve education locations, 72 stops and external hospitals cannot support live outage, coverage, shelter, resource or restoration percentages.

causalTrace.summary: Synthetic causal ledgers reconcile internally but do not cite local boundary conditions, assets, decisions or evidence validity.
notes: Counterfactual and contribution arithmetic is deterministic and auditable as model logic.
Drivers remain generic scenario intensity, demographics and synthetic resilience rather than defence/pump state, rain cell, route closure, fire source/fuel or named operator action.
The trace needs evidence class, publisher/version/time/licence/coverage, affectsSimulation, uncertainty and explicit Unknown/NoData at every transition.

recovery72h.summary: Persistent flood/compound damage and generic recovery are not driven by Nieuwkoop actions, routes or resources.
notes: River remains at 0.191091 stress and 0.605144 depth with 3,876 affected and 475,763.454 deprived person-hours at T+72; no selected defence, pump/dewatering, evacuation or repair explains the state.
Compound remains at 0.551515 stress and 0.548890 depth with 17,933 affected, Telecom 0.176792 and 1,232,915.490 deprived person-hours at T+72, without named decisions/resources.

Pluvial/winter/wildfire forcing clears with generic service recovery; coastal has zero current depth but 3,101 affected at T+72. Neither clearance nor residual impact is backed by inspection, drainage, route, care, suppression or operator completion evidence.
Only confirmed action and evidence-valid authority/operator state should alter recovery; T+72 is a decision checkpoint, not an automatic all-clear.

findings.summary: Official 2025 identity, boundary, places and resident totals reconcile.

findings.action: Retain authoritative identity/boundary, the nine-person reconciliation difference, independent BAG/BRT roles and field-level null semantics. Do not rewrite rounded observations or make thirteen VRHM cores equal a BAG/BRT count.

findings.summary: Coastal and river presets present precise local inundation without a Nieuwkoop defence/hydraulic case.
findings.evidence: Coastal reaches exactly 1.242420 stress-depth and 11,565 affected at T+24; river reaches 0.605144 and 3,876 affected by T+72. Neither selects primary/regional defence, failure/breach, boezem/polder connectivity, terrain, arrival, duration, pumping or dewatering. VRHM distinguishes primary and regional failures; Rijnland documents the separate Ringsloot/boezem/pump chain.
findings.action: Suppress local depth/exposure until a versioned Rijnland/RWS/WMCN/LIWO case selects water boundary, defence/failure, connected cells, AHN datum, depth/velocity, arrival, uncertainty, recession, pumping and dewatering. Separate coastal-primary, regional-boezem and direct-river/indirect-supply cases.

findings.summary: Generic pluvial depth ignores published local stress tests and drainage mechanisms.
findings.evidence: Canonical pluvial T+24 emits 0.532421 depth, 4,882 affected and exact service losses. The municipality documents 60 mm/h and 130 mm/multi-hour 2018 events, core-specific complaints/investigations and outside-area pressure sewers not designed for stormwater, but none enters the model.
findings.action: Integrate the licensed/versioned stress-test rain, terrain/surface flow, buildings/roads, sewer/pressure-system scope, surface water, pump/boezem boundary and calibration events. Render uncovered cells, sewer response and route passability Unknown rather than inferred dry/open.

findings.summary: Five unrelated hazards reuse one exact 37-neighbourhood order and ignore an explicit source.
findings.evidence: River, coastal, pluvial, heat and canonical wildfire share the same first six neighbourhoods in exactly the same order. With wildfire epicentre at the official centre of BU05690102 Nieuwkoop Nieuwkoopse Plassen, that source ranks only 26th of 37 behind the generic leaders.
findings.action: Replace the shared seed with hazard-specific spatial support and source-containment/distance logic: hydraulics, rain/drainage, heat/built form/presence, fire fuel/wind/source and named cyber targets. Add cross-hazard rank-independence and explicit-source regression tests; unsupported cells are Unknown.

findings.summary: The canonical wildfire is external-smoke-only and does not select a local peat/reed fire mechanism.
findings.evidence: Canonical wildfire at T+24 gives zero flame, smoke 0.362637, zero affected residents and 100,358.224 deprived person-hours. VRHM lists peat/reed fires and the province documents Nieuwkoop's peat/lake/Natura 2000 landscape, but no ignition, fuel/moisture, perimeter, wind, visitors, access, firewater or suppression is selected.
findings.action: Keep external smoke and local peat/reed/nature fire as separate named cases. Require versioned land cover/fuels, source/perimeter, event-valid wind/moisture, presence ranges, firewater/access, closures and suppression; zero canonical flame is not proof of no local nature-fire risk.

findings.summary: Drainage/water recovery omits the vulnerable multi-party pumping and boezem chain.
findings.evidence: Rijnland documents daily pumping, roughly 60% underdrainage, private installations, Ringsloot, main pumping and Rijnland boezem. HWH has 332 partial points under three managers, with most surface-pump capacities and all weir/sluice capacities missing. The model nevertheless reports exact drainage/water curves and generic recovery.
findings.action: Represent surface water, sewer/wastewater and drinking water separately; add reviewed aggregate catchments, control direction, compatible units, power/backup, owner/coordination, measured boundary, action state and uncertainty. Never infer operation or restoration from a registered point.

findings.summary: The four-edge graph cannot support dispersed-village evacuation, current closures or route-diverse external acute care.

Local N207/N231, N463, Ringdijk-Hertog van Beijerenstraat, bridges and core streets are omitted. No local acute department exists, and nearest alternatives lie 14.588–19.084 km straight-line away. A valid Zevenhovenseweg closure is not represented by assigned NDW data.
findings.action: Add typed local/core, provincial, bridge, water-crossing, transit and care routes with direction, vehicle class, jurisdiction, valid closure/capacity, alternative and responder-exemption semantics. Model privacy-safe ambulance destination/acceptance/diversion and mutual aid; missing route/care state stays Unknown.

findings.summary: First-72-hour impact and recovery are not driven by accountable local/regional actions and resources.
findings.evidence: River T+72 retains 3,876 affected and 475,763.454 person-hours; compound retains 17,933 affected and 1,232,915.490 person-hours. Short hazards recover generically. No ledger records warning, defence/boezem reconnaissance, private-pump coordination, evacuation/shelter, closure/bridge, boat, ambulance/care, fire suppression, utility repair or resupply.

residualLimitations: No expert-selected Rijnland/RWS/WMCN/LIWO case supplies water boundary, primary/regional defence or breach, connected boezem/polder footprint, depth/velocity, arrival, duration, recession and dewatering for GM0569.
Municipal climate-stress outputs are documented but their machine layer, exact rainfall/heat/drought scenario, edition, CRS/resolution, reuse licence, coverage and NoData are not integrated.

The 332 HWH objects have partial national coverage and lack complete catchment connectivity, flow direction, compatible units, current level/settings, power/backup and restoration; surface water, sewer/wastewater and drinking water remain separate.

Private underdrainage and multi-party communication/coordination are a documented vulnerability, but no public incident-time status, owner availability, failure, portable pumping or T+72 action feed exists.

Four numbered-road edges omit local village streets, N207/N463 and other cross-region access, bridges/water crossings, vehicle classes, traffic control, responder exceptions and destination throughput; N231 duplicate sections are non-additive.

The Zevenhovenseweg closure is valid through 18 September 2026 according to the current municipal page, but exact machine geometry, direction/access exceptions and subsequent updates require refreshed authority evidence at exercise time.
